title: Tenant Lease Policy and Burst Containment for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Shah
problem_statement: Customers require predictable reserved throughput for Dedicated tenants while still allowing safely bounded burst capacity. Current reserve semantics are all-or-nothing: a tenant either has reserved slots or they are throttled. This leads to poor utilization, brittle deployments during transient spikes, and operational overhead for manual pre-warming and on-call interventions.
goals: Introduce a lease-based reservation model that allows short-term leases (minutes to hours) on reserved capacity to support transient bursts without impacting other tenants' SLAs
Provide automated containment and graceful reclamation when bursts threaten cross-tenant SLOs (soft-fencing + priority decay)
Surface clear billing and telemetry for lease usage, burst credits, and reclaimed headroom
Expose control primitives for customers to set burst budgets, minimum guaranteed throughput, and priority decay rules via API and Console
non_goals: Rewriting the scheduler runtime (this PRD restricts changes to control-plane allocation, not per-GPU kernel selection)
Providing unlimited on-demand burst for free — bursts must be bounded and billable
Replacing existing long-term reserved contract flows (monthly/yearly)
stakeholders: Product: Priya Shah (owner), Marco Lin (ops PM)
Engineering: Serving Runtime (Lead: Sana Iqbal), Capacity Orchestration (Lead: Omar Reyes)
summary_of_solution: Add a lease/escrow layer on top of existing reserved pools. Tenants can request short-term leases with configurable duration, headroom fraction, and credit budget. The control plane will grant leases if capacity headroom permits, track credits, and proactively reclaim or throttle leases when cross-tenant SLO risk is detected. Console and API surfaces will allow configuring defaults, per-lease overrides, and visualization of credit burn. Billing will record lease consumption as a distinct line item.
api_surface: POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/leases - create lease; payload: {tenant_id, target_pool_id, duration_seconds, headroom_pct, credit_limit_tokens, preemptible:true|false}
GET /v1/dedicated/reservations/leases/{lease_id} - status, start_ts, end_ts, consumed_credits, state{ACTIVE,RECLAIMING,RELEASED}
PATCH /v1/dedicated/reservations/leases/{lease_id} - extend or adjust credit_limit_tokens (if policy allows)
POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/leases/{lease_id}:release - voluntary release to free headroom
GET /v1/dedicated/reservations/pools/{pool_id}/headroom - returns available headroom_pct and active_leases
control_plane_behaviour: Leases are advisory to the runtime; the runtime will accept leases only if node-level constraints permit without violating active tenant SLOs

A global risk monitor computes cross-tenant SLO tension every 10s. If tension exceeds threshold, control plane transitions lower-priority leases to RECLAIMING, signalling runtime to gradually drain KV-caches and deny new in-flight requests beyond a soft cap
Escrow credits are consumed per-token; when credits are exhausted the lease transitions to RELEASED
user_stories: As a platform engineer managing a SaaS tenant, I want to request a 30-minute burst lease that allows 2x my reserved throughput so my product can handle marketing traffic without a permanent commitment
As an operator, I want automatic partial reclamation that drains burst capacity over 60 seconds rather than abrupt cutoff, so user-facing latency spikes are minimized
As a finance owner at a customer, I want clear billing records and usage dashboards that show lease credit consumption so I can reconcile costs
functional_requirements: FR-1: Leases must be uniquely addressable and auditable (lease_id, tenant_id, pool_id, created_by, start_ts, end_ts, credit_limit_tokens, consumed_tokens)
FR-2: Admin policy to set maximum headroom percentage per pool (e.g., max_burst_headroom_pct)
FR-3: Tenants may configure default burst budget and per-lease overrides via API and Console
FR-4: System must support lease lifecycle states and transitions: PENDING -> ACTIVE -> RECLAIMING -> RELEASED
FR-5: Control plane will emit events to runtime with 500ms SLO for lease state changes under normal load
FR-6: Billing will record consumed tokens per lease as separate usage dimension within 5 minutes of consumption
non_functional_requirements: NFR-1: Headroom decision path must return within 100ms for API requests under p95 load
NFR-2: Telemetry for leases (count, active, reclaimed, credits) retained for 90 days in Console
NFR-3: Feature rollout must be progressively gated behind feature flags and tenant entitlements
NFR-4: New control-plane components must have automated chaos tests validating reclamation behavior
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Create lease API succeeds and returns lease_id, start_ts and predicted headroom_pct when pool has sufficient headroom
AC-2: When pool headroom insufficient, create lease returns 409 with explanatory code and suggestions (e.g., reduce headroom_pct or try later)
AC-3: Lease transitions to RECLAIMING when global SLO tension > configured threshold and runtime reduces new request acceptance by configured soft_cap within 60s
AC-4: Consumed credits are visible in Console within 2 minutes and in billing exports within 10 minutes

AC-5: A synthetic tenant using a 10-minute lease that requests 3x reserved throughput will be gracefully degraded to baseline within a 90s reclamation window during a simulated cross-tenant SLO breach in the canary environment

AC-6: Integration tests cover lease create/extend/release and billing pipeline recording for edge cases (credit exhaustion during extension, double-release, race between reclaim and voluntary release)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): Internal tenants only; feature flag enabled; run 2 weeks of soak with synthetic traffic; validate ACs
Phase 1 (Early Access): Select customers opt-in via billing entitlements; add explicit console UI; 4-week evaluation window
Phase 2 (General Availability): Open to all Dedicated customers; enable default limits and add monitoring runbooks
Phase 3: Iterate on policies based on telemetry and customer feedback; expose policy templates (aggressive, conservative)
telemetry_and_monitoring: Metrics: active_leases, leases_created_per_minute, leases_reclaimed_per_minute, consumed_lease_tokens_per_minute, average_reclaim_window_seconds
Dashboards: per-pool headroom heatmap, top burst consumers, billing delta by lease
Tracing: correlate lease_id to request traces to debug client-facing latency during reclaim
dependencies_list: Billing pipeline: new usage dimension for lease_token_consumption (Billing team)
Runtime acceptance hooks: small runtime change to accept advisory lease signals (Serving Runtime team)
Console UI components for lease creation and credit visualizations (Design/Frontend)
SLA/risk monitor: global SLO tension service (Reliability team)
Feature flag infra for staged rollout (Plattform)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Leases could be exploited to cause noisy-neighbor issues. Mitigation: strict admin max_headroom_pct per pool, per-tenant burst budgets, and early reclamation with priority decay
Risk: Billing mismatch due to delayed usage export. Mitigation: end-to-end pipeline tests and compensating reconciliation job
Risk: Abrupt poor UX during reclaim. Mitigation: gradual drain windows, console notifications, and client-facing retry hints in SDKs
open_questions: Q1: Default credit unit — should we bill per-token or per-1000-tokens in first release?
Q2: Should preemptible leases be discounted automatically? (finance implication)
Q3: How should leases interact with existing tenant fairshare policies during multislot allocations?
next_steps: Finalize answers to open questions with Finance and Reliability by 2026-03-22
Kickoff architecture spike to validate headroom decision latency and chaos reclaim flow (2 week spike)
Draft Console UX flows and API docs for developer preview
